Rashi on Nazir 26a:1:1.hebrew: שהפרישו מעות לקיניהן - ואח"כ העשירו, כגון מצורע. אם חייבי חטאת ועולה הן — אם רצה להוסיף עליהן ולהביא מהן חטאת בהמה, יביא:
Rashi on Nazir 26a:1:1.english: Who separated money for their nests - And afterwards they became wealthy, such as a metzora. If they are [people] obligated in a sin-offering and a burnt-offering — if he wishes to add to them and bring from them an animal sin-offering, he may bring [it].

Rashi on Nazir 26a:1:2.english: [If] he died and had unallocated funds, they shall fall to a freewill offering - And we are not concerned about the money of the sin-offering that is among them.

Rashi on Nazir 26a:2:1.hebrew: תנא נזיר וחייבי קינין דדמו ליה - דנזיר טמא מביא קינין, והואיל דקי"ל גבי נזיר טמא הכי, אמרי' נמי לגבי נזיר טהור, שאם מת והיו לו מעות סתומין, יפלו לנדבה:
Rashi on Nazir 26a:2:1.english: [The Tanna] taught a nazirite and those obligated [to bring] nests, which are similar to it - For an impure nazirite brings nests; and since it is established for us regarding an impure nazirite thus, we also say regarding a pure nazirite, that if he died and had unallocated funds, they shall fall to [communal] gift offerings.

Rashi on Nazir 26a:2:2.hebrew: ולאפוקי מהא דתניא מי שהיה מחוייב חטאת ואמר הרי עלי עולה לנדבה והפריש מעות ואמר אלו לחובתי רצה להביא בהן חטאת בהמה לא יביא - לפי שיש לומר: שמא שם עולה חל עליהן; ולהביא עולת בהמה אי אפשר, שמא לשם חטאת הפריש אותן המעות, ולית להו תקנה. וקמ"ל דהכי הוא גבי נזיר ודדמי ליה, דחייב בחטאת ובעולה בבת אחת — דהתם הוא דאמר הלכה דיפלו לנדבה; אבל כל היכא דלא נתחייב בחטאת ובעולה על מעשה אחד, לא אמרי' הכי, אלא ילכו לים המלח:
Rashi on Nazir 26a:2:2.english: And to exclude that which is taught [in a baraita]: One who was obligated [to bring] a sin-offering, and said, “Behold, upon me is a burnt-offering” as a freewill offering, and separated money and said, “These are for my obligation” — [if] he wished to bring an animal sin-offering with them, he may not bring [it] - Because there is [reason] to say: perhaps the designation of a burnt-offering took effect upon them; and to bring an animal burnt-offering is impossible, [for] perhaps he separated that money for the sake of a sin-offering — and they have no remedy. And [the tanna] teaches us that this applies regarding a nazirite and whatever is similar to him, who is obligated in a sin-offering and in a burnt-offering at one time, for [only] there did the Halakhah state that they shall fall to freewill offerings; but wherever one did not become obligated in a sin-offering and in a burnt-offering for a single act, we do not say this, but rather they shall go to the Dead Sea.

Rashi on Nazir 26a:2:3.hebrew: ע"א מי שהיה מחוייב חטאת - דהיינו יולדת עשירה, דמביאה חטאת עוף ולא עולת העוף, ואמרה: "הרי עלי עולת העוף", והפרישה מעות ואמרה: "אלו לחובתי". רצתה להוסיף ולהביא חטאת בהמה — לא תביא, דהא אינה מחוייבת חטאת בהמה. רצתה להביא עולת בהמה — לא תביא, שהיא לא נדרה אלא עולת העוף. "מת" — כלומר: מתה — והיו לה מעות סתומים, ילכו לים המלח, משום דאיכא למימר שמא לשם חטאת בלבד הפרישתן, שהרי לא הוקבעו כולן ביחד לחטאת העוף ולעולת העוף, דעל חטאת העוף היה החיוב בפני עצמו ועל עולת העוף היתה נדורה בפני עצמו, דכמפורש דמי. והאי "לאפוקי" — מהאי תנא, דאמר: ילכו לים המלח; אבל גבי שאר חייבי קינין, דחייבים להביא חטאת העוף ועולת העוף, הואיל והוקבעו ביחד, דעל שניהם נתחייבה בבת אחת — הילכך כי מתה והיו לה מעות סתומין, יפלו לנדבה, דהויין סתומין מעליא:
Rashi on Nazir 26a:2:3.english: Another explanation: One who was obligated [to bring] a sin-offering - That is, a wealthy woman after childbirth, who brings a bird sin-offering and not a bird burnt-offering, and she said: "It is incumbent upon me [to bring] a bird burnt-offering," and she separated money and said: "These are for my obligation." [If] she wished to add [funds] and bring an animal sin-offering, she may not bring [one], for she is not obligated in an animal sin-offering. [If] she wished to bring an animal burnt-offering, she may not bring [one], since she vowed only a bird burnt-offering. [If] "he died" — that is to say, she died — and she had unallocated funds, they shall go to the Dead Sea, because it can be said: Perhaps she separated them solely for the sake of the sin-offering; for they were not designated together for [both] the bird sin-offering and the bird burnt-offering, since for the bird sin-offering the obligation was on its own, and for the bird burnt-offering she was bound by a vow on its own, so it is considered as [funds that are already] allocated. And this [teaching of the Gemara that our Mishnah comes] to exclude is [to exclude the view of] this Tanna, who said: They shall go to the Dead Sea. But regarding other [individuals] obligated in bird-nests, who are obligated to bring [both] a bird sin-offering and a bird burnt-offering — since they were designated together, as she became obligated in both of them at once — therefore, when she died and had unallocated funds, they shall be allocated for gift offerings, as they are genuinely unallocated [funds].

Rashi on Nazir 26a:4:1.hebrew: אמר רב אשי הא דאמרי' - גבי מעות, שאם היו מפורשין דדמי חטאת ילכו לים המלח ודמי עולה יקרבו עולה כו' — לא תימא דלא הוו' מפורשין אי לאו דאמר "אלו לחטאתי", אלא אפילו [אמר] "אלו לחובתי", הרי אלו מפורשין, ודמי חטאת ילכו לים המלח ודמי עולה יקרבו עולה וכו'. והיכי דמי סתומים, דאמר "יפלו לנדבה"? כגון שהפרישן ביחד סתם, ולא הוציא בשפתיו כלום:
Rashi on Nazir 26a:4:1.english: Rav Ashi said: That which we said - regarding money, that if it was allocated, the money for the sin-offering shall go to the Dead Sea and the money for the burnt-offering shall be sacrificed as a burnt-offering, etc. — do not say that it is not [considered] allocated unless he said, “These are for my sin-offering [and these for my burnt-offering, etc.];” rather, even [if he said], “These are for my obligatory offerings,” these are [considered] allocated, and the money for the sin-offering shall go to the Dead Sea and the money for the burnt-offering shall be sacrificed as a burnt-offering, etc. And what are the circumstances of unallocated [funds], concerning which [the Mishnah] says, “they shall fall to [a fund for] freewill offerings”? For example, where he set them aside together without specification, and did not utter anything with his lips.

Rashi on Nazir 26a:6:1.english: If the value of a sin-offering fell from among them - If an amount equivalent to the value of a sin-offering was lost or separated from among them.

Rashi on Nazir 26a:6:2.hebrew: הרי הן כמפורשין - והשאר לא יפלו לנדבה, אבל מביא בדמי חציין עולה, ובדמי חציין שלמים בלא לחם:
Rashi on Nazir 26a:6:2.english: They are as allocated - And the remainder does not fall to [freewill] gift-offerings; rather, he brings a burnt-offering with the money of half of them, and a peace-offering without bread with the money of half of them.

Tosafot on Nazir 26a:1:1.hebrew: מת והיו לו מעות סתומין יפלו לנדבה - אע"פ שדמי חטאת מעורבין בהן:
Tosafot on Nazir 26a:1:1.english: "If he died and he had unallocated funds, they shall fall to gift offerings" - Even though money for a sin-offering is mixed in with them.

Tosafot on Nazir 26a:2:1.hebrew: תני נזיר וכל דדמי ליה - י"מ דהלכה כך נשנית: "נזיר וכל דדמי ליה". וא"ת: במאי דמי לנזיר? שמביאין על דבר אחד שני קרבנות, כמו נזיר על נזירותו; ויולדת ומצורע שמביאים גם הם על ד"א ב' קרבנות:
Tosafot on Nazir 26a:2:1.english: "He taught: A nazirite and all that is similar to him" - Some explain that the halakha was taught thus: "A nazirite and all that is similar to him." And if you say: In what way is [this] similar to a nazirite? [It is] that they bring two offerings for a single matter, like a nazirite for his naziriteship; and a woman after childbirth and a leper also bring two offerings for a single matter.

Tosafot on Nazir 26a:2:2.hebrew: ולאפוקי מהאי תנא - כלומר, ר' יוחנן דקאמר "הלכה היא בנזיר", דמשמע בנזיר ולא דבר אחר — לאפוקי מהאי תנא, דתניא: מי שמחוייב חטאת שאכל חלב, ואמר: "הרי עלי עולה" — דהיינו נדבה, והרי הוא מחוייב חטאת ועולה, [וחטאת] לא [על] דבר אחד הן, שהחטאת בא על החלב והעולה בנדר — והפריש מעות, ואמר (בשם) כשהפריש: "אלו לחובתי", ומשמע לכל מה שהיה חייב; לפיכך, אם רצה להביא בכולן חטאת בהמה — לא יביא, עולת בהמה — לא יביא, מפני שהן מעורבין, ואין לו תקנה עד שיביא ב' בהמות ויאמר: "כל מה שיש במעות אלו לקדושת חטאת יחול על בהמה זו". וצ"ע: דמאי שנא דלעיל גבי הפריש מעות, רצה להביא חטאת בהן — יביא, עולה — יביא, ולא אמרינן דהפרשה היתה לשניהם דוקא, אלא בידו להביא מכולן (אלא) או חטאת או עולה? וכן לעיל, כי מפריש מעות לנזירותו, אמר: "מפני שראויין להביא בכולן שלמים"! ושמא י"ל: כי אמר בלשון זה "לחובתי", משמע לכל מה שהוא חייב, הילכך הפרשה היתה לשניהם ולא יוכל להביא בכולן אחד מהם; אבל לנזירותו או לצרעתו, משמע שפיר למקצת נזירותו או למקצת צרעתו. ועוד יש לחלק: היכא דהפריש לנזירותו או לצרעתו, וכל קרבנות נזיר ויולדת וצרעת בני חד בקתא (יוצאה), לכך יכול להביא מתחילה מכל דמי הקן פרידה אחת — או חטאת או עולה; הילכך כשהעשיר, מביא מכולן או חטאת או עולה. אבל הכא, דמחוייב חטאת מחלב שאכל ועולה נדורה, לאו בני חד בקתא אינון, וכשמפריש מעות לשמם — אין יכול להביא מכולן אחת מהן:
Tosafot on Nazir 26a:2:2.english: "And to exclude [the view of] this Tanna" - That is to say, R. Yochanan, who said: "It is a halakhah regarding a nazirite," which implies specifically regarding a nazirite and not another matter, [comes] to exclude [the view of] this Tanna [of the baraita]. For it is taught [in a baraita]: One who was obligated in a sin-offering because he ate forbidden fat, and said, "It is incumbent upon me [to bring] a burnt-offering," which is a voluntary gift, and thus he is obligated in a sin-offering and a burnt-offering, and [they] are not for a single matter, as the sin-offering comes for the forbidden fat and the burnt-offering through a vow; and he separated money and said when he separated [them]: "These are for my obligation," which implies for all that he was obligated in. Therefore, if he wished to bring an animal sin-offering with all of them, he may not bring [it]; [if he wished to bring] an animal burnt-offering, he may not bring [it], because they are mixed together. And he has no remedy until he brings two animals and says: "Whatever in this money belongs to the sanctity of a sin-offering shall take effect upon this animal..." And it requires further examination: For how is this different from earlier (26a:1) regarding one who separated money [for nests, where the baraita teaches]: If he wished to bring an animal sin-offering with them, he may bring [it], [or if he wished to bring] a burnt-offering, he may bring [it], and we do not say that the designation was specifically for both of them, but rather it is within his power to bring from all of them either a sin-offering or a burnt-offering? And similarly earlier (25a), when one separates money for his naziriteship, [the Gemara] said: "Because they are fit to bring peace-offerings with all of them"! And perhaps one can say: When he said with this wording, "for my obligation," it implies for all that he owes; therefore, the designation was for both of them, and he cannot bring one of them with all of them. But "for his naziriteship" or "for his tzara'at" can well imply for part of his naziriteship or for part of his tzara'at. And furthermore, one can distinguish: Where one separated [money] for his naziriteship or for his tzara'at — and all the offerings of a nazirite, a woman after childbirth, and a metzora are "of one flock" (i.e., part of a single, unified obligation) — therefore, he can from the outset bring a single bird, either a sin-offering or a burnt-offering, from all the funds of the nest; therefore, when he becomes wealthy, he brings either a sin-offering or a burnt-offering from all of them. But here, where he is obligated in a sin-offering for the forbidden fat that he ate and a vowed burnt-offering, they are not "of one flock," and when he separates money for their designation, he cannot bring one of them from all of them:

Tosafot on Nazir 26a:3:1.hebrew: מת והיו לו מעות סתומים ילכו לים המלח וכו' - דכיון דלא מייתי חטאת ועולה אחד מילתא, לא גמירי בה הילכתא דיפלו לנדבה, אלא כשהחטאת והעולה באין בשביל דבר א'. אבל היכא שהחטאת באה על החלב והעולה נדורה — לא גמירי בה דיפלו לנדבה:
Tosafot on Nazir 26a:3:1.english: If he died and had unallocated funds, they shall go to the Dead Sea, etc. - For since he does not bring a sin-offering and a burnt-offering on account of one matter, the halakha was not transmitted regarding it that they should fall to gift offerings, but rather only when the sin-offering and the burnt-offering come on account of one matter. However, where the sin-offering comes for [eating forbidden] fat and the burnt-offering is a vowed offering, it was not transmitted regarding it that they should fall to gift offerings.

Tosafot on Nazir 26a:4:1.hebrew: הא דאמרת מפורשים לא - ששנינו במשניות: "דמי חטאת ילכו לים המלח וכו'", ולא אמרי' יפלו כולן לנדבה; לא תימא דוקא "אלו לחטאתי", כגון שהפריש ג' צבורין, כל אחד בפני עצמו, אבל בצבור אחד — נדבה, אלא אפי' שהפריש בצבור אחד ואמר "אלו יהא לחטאתי ולשלמי ולעולתי", ולא הפרידם כלל — מפורשין הן. פי': מפורשים בתערובות, ולא נישנית בהן ההלכה דנימא כיון דדמי חטאת מעורבין בהם יפלו לנדבה, אלא אדרבה, כולן ילכו לים המלח. ולאו היינו דין דמפורשין דמתניתין, דקאמר דעולה תקרב עולה, דהתם מבוררין הן — מבוררין דמים הללו לחטאת והללו לשלמים, כל אחד קרב כדינו, ודמי חטאת לים המלח. ולהאי לישנא, כי גמירי דסתומים יפלו לנדבה, היינו כי אמר "אלו לחובתי". הגה"ה: יש לתת טעם בדבר: כשאמר "לקרבנות נזירותי", הוו סתומין גמורין, שאין במשמעות לשונו חטאת יותר משאר קרבנות; דכמו שהחטאת באה לחובה, כך עולה לחובה ולא לנדבה. הגה"ה: איכא דאמרי, כי אמר "לחובתי" נמי כמפורשין בתערובות הן, וילכו לים המלח; ד"לחובתי" משמע לכל חובתי, בין לחטאת בין לעולה. וסתומים דיפלו לנדבה, היינו כי אמר "לקרבנות נזירותי", שלא פירש חטאת בהן; ומ"מ משמע נמי דלכל קרבנות קאמר, ולא היה יכול להביא בכולן קרבן א'. אבל אמר "לנזירותי" גרידא, שלא הזכיר קרבנות, יוכל להביא בכולן קרבן א', דלמקצת נזירותו משמע; ואם מת — הלכה נתקבלה בנזיר "יפלו לנדבה", שהרי יכול להביא בכולן עולה. וקשה: דא"כ, כי אמר "לחובתי" דילכו לים המלח, ואפי' בנזיר, וא"כ מאי האי דקאמר לעיל: "ולאפוקי מהאי תנא כו'"? וכיון דההוא תנא איירי כגון דקאמר "לחובתי", מהא מסייעו דילכו לים המלח! והלא גם בנזירות נמי, כי אמר "לחובתי", אמרי' להאי לישנא דילכו לים המלח! בשלמא לפי' ר"ת ניחא, אלא לפי' רש"י מאי מפקא? וי"ל: דסיפא דברייתא לעיל מפקא, דקתני: "מת והיו לו מעות סתומין" — שלא הזכיר עליהם "לחובתי", אלא אמר "אלו יהיו לקרבנותי" — ילכו לים המלח. דאי ארישא דוקא קאי, היכא דאמר "לחובתי", לימא "מת — ילכו לים המלח"; דמאי האי דקאמר "מת והיו לו מעות סתומין"? והא ברישא נמי בסתומין קיימי! אלא ודאי אתי למימר סתומים אחריני שלא הזכיר ברישא; דברישא איירי דאמר "לחובתי", וסיפא אתי למימר דאפילו כי אמר "לקרבנותי" — דילכו לים המלח, וכה"ג, כי אמר "לקרבנות נזירותי" — יפלו לנדבה:
Tosafot on Nazir 26a:4:1.english: "That which you said, allocated, no" - As we learned in the Mishnayot: "The money for a sin-offering shall go to the Dead Sea, etc.," and we do not say that all of it shall fall to voluntary gift offerings; do not say [that it means] specifically [where he said,] "These are for my sin-offering" [and these for my burnt-offering, etc.], such as where he separated three piles, each one by itself, but in [the case of] one pile [they would fall to] gift offerings; rather, even where he separated [them] in one pile and said, "These shall be for my sin-offering, and for my peace-offerings, and for my burnt-offering," and did not divide them at all, they are [considered] allocated. Explanation: [They are considered] allocated in a mixture, and the halakha was not taught regarding them to say that since the money for a sin-offering is mixed into them, they shall fall to gift offerings; rather, on the contrary, all of it must go to the Dead Sea. And this is not the rule of "allocated" in the Mishnah, which says that the burnt-offering shall be sacrificed as a burnt-offering [and peace-offerings as peace-offerings], for there they are distinct — this money is clearly designated for a sin-offering and this for peace-offerings, [so] each one is sacrificed according to its law, and the sin-offering money goes to the Dead Sea. And according to this version, when it was learned [as a halakhic tradition] that unallocated funds fall to gift offerings, that is when he said, "These are for my obligation." Gloss: A rationale can be provided for this matter: When he said, "for the offerings of my naziriteship," they are completely unallocated, as there is no indication in the meaning of his words of a sin-offering any more than the other offerings; for just as the sin-offering comes as an obligation, so too the burnt-offering comes as an obligation, and not as a voluntary gift. Gloss: [According to the second version of Rav Ashi, which states] "Some say," when he said "for my obligation" they are also considered allocated in a mixture and must go to the Dead Sea, for "for my obligation" implies for all my obligations, whether for a sin-offering or for a burnt-offering. And unallocated [funds] that fall to gift offerings is when he said, "for the offerings of my naziriteship," in which he did not specify a sin-offering; and nevertheless, it also implies that he meant for all [his] offerings, and he could not have brought a single offering from all of them [during his lifetime]. However, if he said merely "for my naziriteship," without mentioning "offerings," he could bring a single offering from all of them, for it implies for part of his naziriteship; and if he died, the halakha was received regarding a nazirite that "they shall fall to gift offerings," for behold, he could have brought a burnt-offering from all of them. And this is difficult: For if so, that when he said "for my obligation" they go to the Dead Sea, even in [the case of] a nazirite, if so, what is that which [the Gemara] said above [26a:2]: "And to exclude [the view of] that Tanna, etc."? And since that Tanna is dealing with [a case] such as where he said "for my obligation," [did the Gemara] cite support from that [baraita] that they go to the Dead Sea?! But behold, in naziriteship as well, when he said "for my obligation," according to this version we say that they go to the Dead Sea! Granted, according to the explanation of Rabbeinu Tam it is well; but according to Rashi's explanation, what does it exclude? And one can say that it excludes the latter clause of the baraita above, which taught: "If he died and he had unallocated funds" — where he did not mention regarding them "for my obligation," but rather said, "These shall be for my offerings" — they shall go to the Dead Sea. For if it referred specifically to the first clause, where he said "for my obligation," let it [simply] say: "[If] he died, they shall go to the Dead Sea." For why does it say: "[If] he died and had unallocated funds"? Behold, in the first clause as well we are dealing with unallocated funds! Rather, it certainly comes to state [a case of] different unallocated funds that were not mentioned in the first clause; for the first clause deals with where he said "for my obligation," and the latter clause comes to state that even when he said "for my offerings," they shall go to the Dead Sea, whereas in such a case [for a nazirite], when he said "for the offerings of my naziriteship," they fall to gift offerings.

Tosafot on Nazir 26a:6:1.hebrew: אמר רבא הא דאמרן סתומין יפלו לנדבה אם נפלה דמי חטאת מביניהם [הוה] - כמו שהפריש מן קצת הצבור, ואמר: "אלו לחטאת, והשאר לשאר נזירותי — לעולה ולשלמים", ומת — הרי שאר המעות כמפורשין; ואף שהן סתומים, בהא לא אמרי' דיפלו כולן לנדבה, אלא יביא חציין לעולה וחציין לשלמים, והלכה לא נשנית אלא כשדמי חטאת מעורבין בהן. וא"ת: התינח לר' יוחנן, דאמר "הלכה בנזיר", אומר דכך נתקבלה ההלכה; אלא לר"ש בן לוי, דדריש קרא דמותר נדר לנדבה — אפילו אין דמי חטאת מעורבין בהן יפלו לנדבה, דהאי נמי מותר נדר הוא, דכל קרבנות נזיר בנדר הם באים! וי"ל, דסברא הוא להעמיד קרא כשדמי חטאת מעורבים בהן דוקא, דהכי משכחת בעלמא דמותר חטאת בא לנדבה, כדאמר בפ' ולד חטאת (תמורה דף כג:) ובזבחים בפרק טבול יום (זבחים דף קג.): "זה מדרש דרש יהוידע הכהן: 'אשם הוא' — לכהן; 'אשם הוא לה'' — להביא כל דבר הבא ממותר אשם ממותר חטאת, ילקח בהם בהמה, והבשר לבעלים והעורות לכהנים". ולפי שמצינו בעלמא דמותר חטאת באין לנדבה, סברא להעמיד זה הפסוק היכא שהפריש מעות ודמי חטאת מעורבין בהן:
Tosafot on Nazir 26a:6:1.english: Rava said: That which we said, that unallocated [funds] will fall to gift offerings — if the money for the sin-offering fell from among them, [it is] - For example, where he separated [money] from part of the pile and said, "These are for the sin-offering, and the rest is for the remainder of my naziriteship — for the burnt-offering and for the peace-offering," and he died, the remaining money is considered as allocated. And even though they are unallocated [between the burnt-offering and the peace-offering], in this [case] we do not say that they should all fall to gift offerings; rather, he brings half of them for a burnt-offering and half of them for a peace-offering. For the halakha was only taught when the money for the sin-offering is mingled with them. And if you say: Granted according to Rabbi Yoḥanan, who said [that it is an oral] halakha with regard to a nazirite, one can say that this is how the halakha was received; but according to Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish [text: ben Levi], who expounds the verse [to mean] that the surplus of a vow [goes] to a gift offering, even if the money for the sin-offering is not mingled with them, they should fall to a gift offering, for this too is the surplus of a vow, since all the offerings of a nazirite come through a vow! And one can say: It is logical to establish the verse specifically when the money for the sin-offering is mingled with them, for so we find generally, that the surplus of a sin-offering goes to a gift offering, as [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Velad Ḥattat (Temurah 23b) and in Zevachim in the chapter [entitled] Tevul Yom (Zevachim 103a): "This was an exposition expounded by Jehoiada the Priest: 'It is a guilt-offering' — to the priest; 'it is a guilt-offering to the Lord' — to include anything that comes from the surplus of a guilt-offering [or] from the surplus of a sin-offering, that an animal shall be purchased with them, and the meat is for the owner and the hides are for the priests." And since we find elsewhere that the surplus of a sin-offering goes to gift offerings, it is logical to establish this verse where he separated money and the money for the sin-offering was mingled with them.
